title: Composition Rug Guide: Sizes, Prices & Teacher Names
meta_description: Composition notebook, math and calm corner rugs for teachers, from 1.6 ft to 6x6 ft. See which size fits your group and what to check before ordering.
body_html:
A composition rug is a classroom rug designed to look like a composition notebook cover, and it often has the teacher's name on it. Which size and build you need depends on how many kids sit on it at once and what kind of floor it goes on.

On this page

  • What is a composition notebook rug, and how is it different from a math rug or calm corner rug?
  • What size classroom rug do I need for my number of students?
  • Will the rug stay put, and can it go outside?
  • Personalizing rugs for teachers: names, wording and a matching tapestry
  • Rugs for the classroom door and the teacher's lounge
  • Worked example: one small-group math corner, start to finish

What is a composition notebook rug, and how is it different from a math rug or calm corner rug?

A composition notebook rug borrows the look of the classic notebook cover and usually has room for the teacher's name. The design works for any subject. A math rug and a calm corner rug each do a narrower job.

Our Teacher Rugs collection has 54 products, priced from $21.90 to $156.85. They fall into three design families:

  • Composition notebook rugs mark the room as yours. The White Doodle Teacher Name Rug shows "Mrs Smith" in pastel letters and starts at $31.90.
  • Math rugs mark a subject or a station. The Problem Solve Math Classroom Rug, the Welcome to Math Class rug with a teacher name, and the MATH acronym rug with a name all start at $31.90.
  • Calm corner rugs mark a spot where kids go to settle. The Personalized Calm Corner Activity Rug starts at $31.90. The Black Emotion Classroom Rug is listed in the composition notebook range, but its title mentions "Feel Can" prompts and feelings artwork, so it could also work in a calm corner.

How to apply it: finish this sentence: "Kids will see this rug and know ______." If the answer is "whose room this is," pick a composition rug. If it's "this is where we do math," pick a math rug. If it's "this is where I go to calm down," pick a calm corner rug. If you need two of these, you probably need two rugs.

What to check

  • What the rug is for, written down before you browse
  • Whether the design has a space for your name (not all of them do; see the personalization section)
  • Whether the wording on the rug suits the age group you teach
  • Whether it repeats something already on your walls

What size classroom rug do I need for my number of students?

Choose the size by how many kids sit on the rug at the same time, not by the number on your class list. A small-group math rug might only ever hold a handful of kids, even in a full class. The square rugs are labeled by how many kids they seat, which makes this the easiest decision on the page.

Some designs come in rectangular sizes instead:

  • 24"x36": from $31.90
  • 36"x60", 48"x72" and 60"x96": the price appears when you choose the size on the product page

How to apply it: count the most kids who will sit on the rug at one time, then find the first row whose seating label covers that number. Mark the size on your floor with painter's tape before you order. Then check that a door can swing open past it and that there's still room to walk around it with a chair pulled out.

What to check

  • The most kids on the rug at once, not your total class size
  • A taped outline on the actual floor at the size you're considering
  • Clearance for door swing and walkways
  • Whether the design you want comes in square sizes, rectangular sizes, or both

Will the rug stay put, and can it go outside?

Don't assume every rug in the collection has the same build. Across the 54 product pages, the features are listed this often:

  • Non-slip backing: "Non-slip neoprene rubber backing" appears on 45 of 54 pages
  • Personalization: "Personalizable with a teacher's name" appears on 45 of 54 pages
  • Indoor and outdoor use: "Suitable for indoor and outdoor use" appears on 21 of 54 pages
  • Cushioning: "Soft sponge memory foam construction for comfort" appears on 16 of 54 pages

These are counts of what each page says, so a feature you care about is only confirmed on pages that state it. Fewer than half the pages mention outdoor use, and fewer than a third mention memory foam.

How to apply it: write down your floor type (tile, vinyl, sealed concrete or carpet) and where the rug goes. Then open the product page and look for the exact line above that matters to you. On a hard floor, look for the neoprene backing line. If kids will sit on it for long stretches, look for the memory foam line. If it's for a covered entrance or an outdoor reading spot, look for the indoor and outdoor line.

What to check

  • Your floor type, written down
  • The "Non-slip neoprene rubber backing" line on the product page, if the floor is hard
  • The "Suitable for indoor and outdoor use" line, if the rug will be outside even part of the time
  • The memory foam line, if cushioning matters for how long kids sit

Personalizing rugs for teachers: names, wording and a matching tapestry

Most rugs for teachers here can carry your name: 45 of the 54 product pages say "Personalizable with a teacher's name." Several featured designs are built around it. The White Doodle rug shows "Mrs Smith" as its sample text. The Custom MATH Acronym Classroom Rug puts a teacher's name alongside the subject. So does the Welcome to Math Class rug.

Some designs also ask, "Would you like to complete the look with a matching tapestry?" On those listings, choosing No starts at $31.90 and choosing Yes starts at $51.85.

This guide doesn't cover three things that matter for a printed name: how many characters the name field takes, whether you see a preview before printing, and whether a personalized order can be changed or returned. Check the product page and the store's policy pages for those before you order.

How to apply it: type your name exactly the way kids say it, title included ("Mrs", "Ms", "Mr", "Dr") and with the punctuation you want. Read it once out loud. If you share the room with a co-teacher, decide whether one name or both go on the rug before you order.

What to check

  • That "Personalizable with a teacher's name" appears on the page for the design you picked
  • Spelling, title and punctuation, typed exactly as you want them printed
  • Whether you want the matching tapestry, which starts at $51.85 on listings that offer it
  • The size of the rug against how long your name is (a long name on a 2x2 ft rug will print smaller)

Rugs for the classroom door and the teacher's lounge

Doormats are the cheapest items in the collection. A blank doormat with no customization starts at $21.90, and a customized doormat starts at $28.90. They come in three sizes, and the starting price depends on the listing:

  • 24"x16" (40x60 cm): from $21.90 on some listings, $25.89 on others
  • 32"x20" (50x80 cm): from $27.89 on some listings, $30.90 on others
  • 36"x24" (60x90 cm): from $33.89 on some listings, $34.90 on others

A mat at the classroom door gets the most foot traffic of anything in the room. A mat in the teacher's lounge mostly just has to look like it belongs there. Either way, the size depends on the doorway, not on how many people use the room.

How to apply it: measure the width of the door opening. Choose the doormat size closest to that width without going wider than the door frame. If the door opens onto an outdoor walkway or a hallway open to the weather, only consider listings that say "Suitable for indoor and outdoor use."

What to check

  • The door opening width, measured in inches
  • Blank ($21.90) or customized ($28.90): decide whether the mat needs your name or room number
  • The indoor and outdoor line, for any door that opens to the weather
  • The backing line, if the mat sits on tile or polished concrete

Worked example: one small-group math corner, start to finish

This is a made-up situation used to show the steps. It isn't a customer story.

A third-grade teacher wants a rug for a small-group math table and a mat for the classroom door.

  1. Purpose. "Kids will see this rug and know this is where we do math." That rules out composition rugs and calm corner rugs, which leaves the math rugs.
  2. Headcount. The whole class never sits there together. The math group never has more than four kids. In the size table, 4x4 ft (M, 3–4 kids) is the first row that covers four.
  3. Floor test. A taped 4x4 ft outline leaves room on every side to pull chairs back, and the door swings past the tape without catching it.
  4. Build. The floor is vinyl tile, so the teacher only keeps math rug pages that say "Non-slip neoprene rubber backing." The group sits for most of a lesson, so they also look for the memory foam line and accept that fewer designs list it.
  5. Name. They choose the MATH acronym rug with a name and type "Mr. Alvarez" exactly as the kids say it. They skip the matching tapestry, so the No option applies.
  6. Door mat. The door opening is a little wider than 32 inches, so the 32"x20" size fits inside the frame. The door opens onto an indoor hallway, so the indoor and outdoor line doesn't matter. They choose a customized doormat.

Starting prices: the 4x4 ft size starts at $59.90 in the collection, and a customized doormat starts at $28.90. Size or option upgrades, tax and shipping are added on top, and the checkout shows those.

If your group is larger than this one, go back to the size table and move down one row. Then compare every composition, math and calm corner design in the collection with your headcount and floor type written down.
